newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's trade gap narrows slightly.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's trade gap narrows slightly.

text.p: Vietnam said on Tuesday its trade gap, a source of increasingly intense debate within the government, had narrowed slightly by mid-October from a record level just a month earlier.
The Statistics Office said the trade deficit for the first 10-1/2 months of this year was $3.35 billion compared with $3.54 billion in the period from January to September 10.
Comparative figures for corresponding periods in 1995 were not published. Nevertheless, the gap between exports and imports is already way above the full-year 1995 figure of $2.3 billion.
The statistics office said exports from the beginning of the year until mid-October were $5.53 billion and imports were $8.88 billion.
The ballooning trade deficit, largely the result of the fast-growing economy's growing appetite for imports, has prompted calls for both an export drive and a curb on imports.
The government recently raised its 1996 export quota for rice by 20 percent to three million tonnes and has made it clear that foreign investment will be chanelled into export-oriented sectors.

Some officials have gone further, advocating an import-substitution policy, and former Foreign Minister Nguyen Co Thach told Reuters at the weekend there were voices within the government pushing for measures to slow trade liberalisation.

The authorities have slashed interest rates this year to encourage the production of goods for export and have given thought to a devaluation of the local currency, the dong, to make it more competitive.
